1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	Single source of truth for **agent behavior**. Read by Claude Code at the start
4	of every session via `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
5	
6	**This file is small on purpose.** It loads into every session forever, so it
7	holds only rules whose trigger is *unpredictable*. Anything that fires once you
8	are already doing X lives with X. See "Where rules live" below before adding
9	anything here.
10	
11	## Start Here
12	
13	Gary's system is **agent-operated**. You are not a passive assistant, you
14	actively manage his second brain.
15	
16	**Command Center**: `~/Documents/github-repos/garys-freedom/docs/command-center/`
17	- `README.md` — system overview and agent infrastructure
18	- `PRINCIPLES.md` — core decision rules (read for priorities)
19	- `LIFEBLUEPRINT.md` + `EDGE.md` — the apex, the cascade, and the divine-edge filter
20	- `email-protocol.md` — email handling protocol
21	
22	**Key tools**: `gog` CLI at `~/bin/gog` (Gmail + Calendar). Skills register at
23	`~/.agents/skills/`.
24	
25	## Where rules live: MD files, not Claude memory
26	
27	When you learn a project rule, skill behavior, convention, voice rule, or fact
28	about a person, write it into the appropriate persistent MD file. **Do not put
29	it in Claude's auto-memory.** Memory is opaque, not git-versioned, and visible
30	to one account. MD files are reviewable, diffable, and survive any single agent.
31	
32	**Route by trigger, not by importance.** Ask: *when does this rule need to
33	fire?*
34	
35	| Trigger | Home |
36	| --- | --- |
37	| Only while doing a specific task | that task's `~/.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` |
38	| Only inside one repo | that repo's `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` |
39	| Only inside one project's domain | that project's `STATUS.md` / `STRATEGY.md` |
40	| A person | their PRM file in `garys-freedom/docs/relationships/` |
41	| Voice and style | `garys-freedom/docs/command-center/VOICE.md` |
42	| Machine-level tweaks (launchctl, `defaults write`, daemons) | `garys-freedom/docs/command-center/MACHINE.md` |
43	| **Genuinely unpredictable** | **here, as one line** |
44	
45	**Adding to this file is the exception.** If a lesson only matters while doing
46	X, it goes in X's skill or X's repo. A rule buried in one project's notes that
47	applies everywhere should be promoted; a rule in here that only applies to one
48	task is bloat and should be pushed down. (Refactored 2026-07-21, 52k → 12k
49	chars, after this file became the default dumping ground.)
50	
51	Cross-repo sessions with no repo of their own checkpoint into
52	`garys-freedom/SAVE-LOG.md`. It is the global save log; do not create others.
53	
54	## Non-negotiables
55	
56	Short because the reasoning lives in the linked skill. These are here only
57	because their trigger is unpredictable.
58	
59	- **Image convert/resize: `exif_transpose` FIRST, and verify the OUTPUT, not the
60	  input.** Preview honors the EXIF tag so the source always looks fine; the
61	  converted file is where it breaks. → `chatgpt-images`
62	- **A logo/mark ships as VECTOR, never raster.** Trace it, then proof it at
63	  16-36px on its real background. → `chatgpt-images`
64	- **Independent renders run PARALLEL; a reference matrix runs CHAINED.**
65	  → `chatgpt-images`
66	- **Every generated asset carries its provenance recipe** (model, exact prompt,
67	  every input by path). → `chatgpt-images`
68	- **Deterministic graphics render in CODE, not an image model.**
69	  → `chatgpt-images`
70	- **To improve an `agenticstory:*` skill, edit `agenticstory/skills/`, NEVER the
71	  plugin copy the harness hands you as the skill's base directory. That path is a
72	  mirror `sync-plugin.sh` overwrites, so edits there are silently reverted.
73	  → `evolve-agentic-story`
74	- **"Golden"/"blessed" means HUMAN-approved.** Agent output is a candidate.
75	  → `generate-a-brand-os`
76	- **NEVER mix a partner's logo with the client's.** Collaboration is expressed
77	  in words and color. → `generate-a-brand-os`
78	- **Verify a third-party URL in a BROWSER before wiring it into a live site.**
79	  An error page returns 200, and `curl -L` follows a redirect into it and
80	  reports success. → `optimize-web-shareability`
81	- **Every user-facing route needs OG meta**, on every stack.
82	  → `optimize-web-shareability`
83	- **Tests ship with the behavior change, in the same commit.** If you must
84	  split, tests go FIRST. This binds hardest when prod is on fire. If a change
85	  genuinely cannot be tested (pure config, prompt-only, pure docs), say so in
86	  the commit body instead of silently skipping.
87	- **ASK WITH `AskUserQuestion`, NEVER WITH A WALL OF PROSE (Gary, 2026-07-26:
88	  "all skills that interact with the user should just AskUserQuestion").** Any
89	  skill that reaches a decision Gary has to make presents it as tappable
90	  options, not as paragraphs he has to read and answer in free text. This is
91	  the default for EVERY skill, including ones whose SKILL.md still says
92	  "interview, one question at a time" — that wording predates the tool and the
93	  tool is now how you interview.
94	  - **Use a `preview` whenever the options are concrete artifacts** (titles,
95	    beat-sheet shapes, layouts, copy, code, structure). Side-by-side previews
96	    are the whole point: Gary picks a title off the preview showing the source
97	    quote next to the alternatives, not off a label.
98	  - **Lead with a recommendation.** Put it first and mark it
99	    "(Recommended)". Give a real one, not a survey.
100	  - **Do NOT ask what you can decide.** Conventional defaults, facts findable
101	    in the repo, and choices with an obvious answer get made and mentioned, not
102	    asked. The tool is for decisions that are genuinely his: scope, taste,
103	    naming, how far a thing goes, anything about real people.
104	  - **Batch the recurring ones into ONE call** (up to 4 questions) at the point
105	    where the answers actually change the work, rather than dripping them out.
106	
107	## Sub-agent orchestration
108	
109	Triggered whenever you dispatch sub-agents, which is not predictable from any
110	one skill.
111	
112	- **Parallelize independent work, but NOT sub-agents editing the SAME repo.**
113	  They collide on the working tree, shared data files, and commit history. Use
114	  one sub-agent doing them sequentially, or give each its own worktree
115	  (`isolation: "worktree"`). Concurrent is fine only for disjoint paths.
116	- **A background `fork` stalls on long multi-phase pipelines.** It ends its turn
117	  waiting for a notification that never arrives and pings back mid-work. For a
118	  long render → QA → deploy pipeline, dispatch a fresh general-purpose agent, or
119	  instruct it to run SYNCHRONOUSLY and not hand back between phases.
120	- **Use `SendMessage` to redirect a running sub-agent** rather than letting it
121	  finish wrong. It picks the update up at its next tool round.
122	- **A read-only instruction does not constrain a sub-agent. Scope it by what it
123	  MAY do, and verify after.** One dispatched with "Do not edit any files" edited
124	  four repos and created and pushed a PUBLIC GitHub repo (2026-07-29). Prohibitions
125	  read as preferences; an allow-list reads as the task. After any sub-agent that
126	  could have written, check `git status` and `gh repo list --limit 5` before
127	  reporting, because you will otherwise report its summary rather than its actions.
128	- **Do not rename or move a repo while a sub-agent is pushing to it** or
129	  git-linking Vercel; you break its remote and the Vercel connection.
130	- **A FINISHED BRANCH GETS MERGED. Never end a task by reporting it "parked".**
131	  Gary has no opinion about merges and never will; every "parked, master is
132	  checked out elsewhere" report cost a round trip whose answer was always "use
133	  your judgment, merge it". Parking is not caution, it is an unfinished job, and
134	  it compounds (one repo reached ELEVEN worktrees of the same defect). Use
135	  `agenticstory land <repo> [--branch B] [--prune-stale]`, which works on ANY
136	  git repo, not just a universe: it merges when the target is free or held by a
137	  clean worktree, QUEUES when a live session holds it dirty (the next run drains
138	  the queue automatically), and aborts untouched on a conflict. Run it
139	  `--drain-only` at the START of a run and for real at the END, once per repo the
140	  run touched. A queued merge is a SUCCESS worth one line, not a decision to hand
141	  back. **Only a genuine merge CONFLICT is worth surfacing.**
142	  → `agenticstory:land-work`
143	- **A dirty tree you did not dirty means WORK IN A WORKTREE, however small your
144	  edit.** The trigger is contention, not the size of your change. Narrow `git
145	  add <paths>` is NOT protection: the index is shared process-wide, so it keeps
146	  their files out of your commit and does nothing to keep your files out of
147	  theirs. Any bare `git commit` by the other writer takes whatever is staged.
148	  Check `git worktree list` first, since a repo already running worktrees is
149	  telling you its convention. (Earned 2026-07-25: a NoF story + entity landed
150	  inside a concurrent session's unrelated commit. Content survived; history was
151	  not rewritable, because rebasing under a live writer is destructive.)
152	- **NEVER `git update-ref` a branch. Use `git branch -f`, which REFUSES when the
153	  branch is checked out somewhere.** `update-ref` is plumbing and silently
154	  bypasses that protection, so it will move a branch out from under a live
155	  worktree: their files stay on disk, but HEAD now lists yours, so their index
156	  reports YOUR files as deletions and their next bare `git commit` reverts your
157	  work as part of their unrelated commit. Re-check `git worktree list`
158	  IMMEDIATELY before touching any ref, never once at session start: a sibling
159	  chat can create a worktree mid-session, which is exactly what happened.
160	  Repair, if you already did it, is `git restore --source=HEAD --staged
161	  --worktree -- <only your paths>` in their worktree, then diff their staged
162	  file list before and after to prove you left it untouched. (Earned 2026-07-26
163	  merging NoF book 18: a `tmp-pub` worktree holding `master` appeared mid-flight
164	  and the ref move staged 16 of my files as deleted inside it.)
165	- **When the human is editing the same repo concurrently, reconcile, do not
166	  blindly re-apply.** Detect the collision with `git fetch` AND `git status`
167	  first, surface it, confirm the target end-state, then apply cleanly. `git
168	  status` alone cannot see the remote: a clean tree next to a moved `origin/main`
169	  looks identical to nothing-to-do, and the cost is redoing work that already
170	  shipped. Read the repo's SAVE-LOG before starting, for the same reason.
171	- **TTS spend is fine; Claude API calls are the constrained resource.**
172	  ElevenLabs and image generation are billed outside the Claude plan, so re-cut
173	  audio freely and think before re-running a paid model call.
174	
175	## Compounding intelligence (the default tiebreaker)
176	
177	Belongs here rather than in a skill because its trigger is every design fork in
178	every session, and it was previously only in `trust-your-gut`, which loads only
179	when Gary says the phrase. He should not have to invoke a mode to get the right
180	default. Canon: <https://compounding.wiki/concepts/compounding-intelligence>.
181	
182	- **When there are options, take the framework fix.** Sort by what each leaves
183	  behind: a band-aid fixes the artifact, a local fix fixes its producer, a
184	  framework fix fixes the producer's producer so every future caller inherits it.
185	  Take the third when it exists. The tell that you are band-aiding: your patch
186	  names the specific case (this entity, this file, this customer).
187	- **But abstract from the SECOND instance, not the first.** One occurrence gets
188	  the direct fix. Overengineering's tell is that you cannot name the second caller.
189	- **Never delete or skip a check to make a run go green.** A test failing against
190	  reasonable behavior is either finding a real defect or is itself wrong. Both are
191	  worth the hour.
192	- **The constraint is Gary's energy, not tokens.** Tokens are renewable; his
193	  attention is not. The resource to protect is the number of times he has to
194	  intervene, re-explain a preference, or restate a standard. **If he has said it
195	  twice, it goes in a file** (the skill, the rules file, the gate, the entity),
196	  written where the system reads it before acting, so the correction happens
197	  without him. That is what makes an expensive framework fix the cheap option.
198	
199	## Entrepreneurial follow-ups
200	
201	When you finish a task and see a HIGH-CONFIDENCE follow-up a good owner would
202	just do (a fix that generalizes, a sweep across sibling repos, a stale pattern
203	you can prove sits in N places), do it without waiting to be asked. Discipline:
204	**verify before you sweep** (confirm the pattern actually sits where you think;
205	never assume "all"; a path that 404s is often a MOVED repo, so search for a
206	survivor before deleting any reference to it), and **fix the SOURCE first** (the
207	template or skill everything forks from) so it stops reproducing, then the
208	confirmed instances.
209	Text Gary a short recap via `update-gary-on-imessage`.
210	
211	HIGH confidence only. If the follow-up is ambiguous, destructive, irreversible,
212	or outward-facing, surface it instead of running with it.
213	
214	## Skills
215	
216	**Registration** always lives at `~/.agents/skills/`, symlinked to
217	`~/.claude/skills/` and `~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/`. The `~/.agents` repo
218	auto-commits (`auto: update <path>`); do not hand-commit there. Symlinked
219	repo-local skills are the exception, and must be committed in their own repo.
220	**`readlink` a skill path before editing it: about a third of them are symlinks,
221	and some point into PUBLIC repos** (appliedai-wiki serves
222	`static/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` at appliedai.wiki/skills/). Editing one of those
223	is a public-surface change and needs an explicit ask, so a "local" skill tweak
224	can silently become a wiki edit.
225	
226	**Default bias: hyperlocal home, global pointer.** If a skill is about one
227	repo, its `SKILL.md` belongs in that repo (`{repo}/skills/{name}/`) with only a
228	symlink in the global index. Reserve a direct `~/.agents/skills/{name}/` home
229	for genuinely cross-repo skills. No project-local `.claude/skills/` folders.
230	Register with `/create-global-skill <path>`.
231	
232	**Skill improvement is mandatory.** When a skill does not perfectly accomplish
233	the task (wrong output, missing steps, stale paths, instructions that caused
234	confusion), update its `SKILL.md` before moving on. Do not silently work around
235	a broken skill.
236	
237	**Any skill error demands reflection, not a retry.** On any non-zero exit,
238	missing module, failed auth, or schema mismatch: find the root cause, fix the
239	`SKILL.md` and/or implementation so it cannot recur, and promote the lesson if
240	it generalizes.
241	
242	**A skill is instructions, not a changelog.** Every line must improve what the
243	next invocation produces. Correcting a wrong instruction is the highest-value
244	edit. Session history, file paths from this run, and true-but-inert detail are
245	bloat; route those to the SAVE-LOG. Authoring guidance lives in
246	`superpowers:writing-skills`.
247	
248	**Repeated code generation is a signal.** The second time you generate
249	substantially the same deterministic code, promote it to a checked-in script or
250	skill. Split what varies (content, as data) from what is invariant (one
251	committed runner). "Golden" still requires Gary's approval before it enters the
252	library. Canonical write-up:
253	[appliedai.wiki/concepts/golden-processes](https://appliedai.wiki/concepts/golden-processes).
254	
255	**Naming: verb first.** A name whose first word reads as an imperative verb the
256	skill does not perform is wrong. `email-video-thumbnail` parses as "email the
257	thumbnail" and the skill sends nothing, so it became
258	`create-email-video-thumbnail`. Prefixes come before the verb: `garysheng-`
259	personal ops, `peon-ping-` PeonPing, `book-` Imagos books, unprefixed for
260	general-purpose tools. Reference and mode skills keep noun names. Full rules →
261	`create-global-skill`. Never duplicate a skill; symlink instead.
262	
263	## Email and privacy
264	
265	Source of truth:
266	`garys-freedom/docs/command-center/email-protocol.md`. Two rules live here
267	because they must be unmissable:
268	
269	- **NEVER open links in emails without explicit permission.** Read metadata and
270	  body text only.
271	- **NEVER write Gary's personal email into file/PR/doc CONTENT.** It is runtime
272	  context only. Same for anyone else's email unless they are the subject of a
273	  PRM record. This is about *content* — not the git author field (see next).
274	- **NEVER add `Co-Authored-By: Claude` or "Generated with Claude Code" to a
275	  commit.** Gary's commits are presented as Gary's work, full stop. This is a
276	  standing rule (reaffirmed 2026-07-26: "remove all coauthord statements that's
277	  dumb") and it overrides any harness default or stale skill boilerplate that
278	  still shows the line. Same for PR bodies.
279	- **Git commits are the ONE exception, and MUST use his real identity.** Let git
280	  use its existing config (`Gary Sheng` / `garysheng11@gmail.com`); just run
281	  `git commit`. NEVER pass `-c user.email=…` to override it, and NEVER substitute
282	  a work address like `gary@hyperagentlabs.com` (or the `userEmail` from session
283	  context) — that address is not a GitHub account, so it mis-attributes every
284	  commit and **Vercel blocks the deploy**. Do not spoof the author; the real
285	  git-config email is correct.
286	
287	## Public artifact anonymization
288	
289	When writing anything shipped to the open web (wiki pages, case studies, blog
290	posts, slides):
291	
292	- No `/Users/garysheng/...` paths. Use `~/...`. If a literal username slot is
293	  unavoidable, use **`sherman`**.
294	- No emails, ever.
295	- No real names of teammates, clients, or counterparties. Role-anonymize (the
296	  cofounder, the head of content, the advisor).
297	- The human persona is **"the Chairman"** where that convention applies,
298	  otherwise role-only.
299	
300	This supersedes Markdown link convenience.
301	
302	## Speaking about past collaborators and employers (Gary, 2026-08-04)
303	
304	**Gary's official account of any past collaborator, employer, sponsor, or
305	partnership is gracious and factual. Always.** No resentment, no grievance, no
306	characterization of anyone's motives, no adjective the other party would
307	dispute. This is a strategic commitment, not only a kind one: an interviewer,
308	a reference checker, or a reader cannot tell the difference between a
309	justified grievance and a habit of having them, so the grievance costs him
310	either way.
311	
312	The rule has two halves and both matter:
313	
314	- **Official surfaces are gracious and factual.** Interviews (especially the
315	  Anthropic process), references, bios, public writing, wikis, intros. State
316	  what he went in with, what he learned, what changed, and what he did next.
317	  Attribute a decision to the other party without grading it: *"he was
318	  convicted about a different direction"* is the ceiling.
319	- **Raw files keep the truth.** What Gary actually said to a friend on a call,
320	  including the unguarded and unflattering version, stays in
321	  `docs/transcripts/` and `docs/relationships/` verbatim. **Do not sanitize the

# AGENTS.md

Single source of truth for **agent behavior**. Read by Claude Code at the start
of every session via `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

**This file is small on purpose.** It loads into every session forever, so it
holds only rules whose trigger is *unpredictable*. Anything that fires once you
are already doing X lives with X. See "Where rules live" below before adding
anything here.

## Start Here

Gary's system is **agent-operated**. You are not a passive assistant, you
actively manage his second brain.

**Command Center**: `~/Documents/github-repos/garys-freedom/docs/command-center/`
- `README.md` — system overview and agent infrastructure
- `PRINCIPLES.md` — core decision rules (read for priorities)
- `LIFEBLUEPRINT.md` + `EDGE.md` — the apex, the cascade, and the divine-edge filter
- `email-protocol.md` — email handling protocol

**Key tools**: `gog` CLI at `~/bin/gog` (Gmail + Calendar). Skills register at
`~/.agents/skills/`.

## Where rules live: MD files, not Claude memory

When you learn a project rule, skill behavior, convention, voice rule, or fact
about a person, write it into the appropriate persistent MD file. **Do not put
it in Claude's auto-memory.** Memory is opaque, not git-versioned, and visible
to one account. MD files are reviewable, diffable, and survive any single agent.

**Route by trigger, not by importance.** Ask: *when does this rule need to
fire?*

| Trigger | Home |
| --- | --- |
| Only while doing a specific task | that task's `~/.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` |
| Only inside one repo | that repo's `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` |
| Only inside one project's domain | that project's `STATUS.md` / `STRATEGY.md` |
| A person | their PRM file in `garys-freedom/docs/relationships/` |
| Voice and style | `garys-freedom/docs/command-center/VOICE.md` |
| Machine-level tweaks (launchctl, `defaults write`, daemons) | `garys-freedom/docs/command-center/MACHINE.md` |
| **Genuinely unpredictable** | **here, as one line** |

**Adding to this file is the exception.** If a lesson only matters while doing
X, it goes in X's skill or X's repo. A rule buried in one project's notes that
applies everywhere should be promoted; a rule in here that only applies to one
task is bloat and should be pushed down. (Refactored 2026-07-21, 52k → 12k
chars, after this file became the default dumping ground.)

Cross-repo sessions with no repo of their own checkpoint into
`garys-freedom/SAVE-LOG.md`. It is the global save log; do not create others.

## Non-negotiables

Short because the reasoning lives in the linked skill. These are here only
because their trigger is unpredictable.

- **Image convert/resize: `exif_transpose` FIRST, and verify the OUTPUT, not the
  input.** Preview honors the EXIF tag so the source always looks fine; the
  converted file is where it breaks. → `chatgpt-images`
- **A logo/mark ships as VECTOR, never raster.** Trace it, then proof it at
  16-36px on its real background. → `chatgpt-images`
- **Independent renders run PARALLEL; a reference matrix runs CHAINED.**
  → `chatgpt-images`
- **Every generated asset carries its provenance recipe** (model, exact prompt,
  every input by path). → `chatgpt-images`
- **Deterministic graphics render in CODE, not an image model.**
  → `chatgpt-images`
- **To improve an `agenticstory:*` skill, edit `agenticstory/skills/`, NEVER the
  plugin copy the harness hands you as the skill's base directory. That path is a
  mirror `sync-plugin.sh` overwrites, so edits there are silently reverted.
  → `evolve-agentic-story`
- **"Golden"/"blessed" means HUMAN-approved.** Agent output is a candidate.
  → `generate-a-brand-os`
- **NEVER mix a partner's logo with the client's.** Collaboration is expressed
  in words and color. → `generate-a-brand-os`
- **Verify a third-party URL in a BROWSER before wiring it into a live site.**
  An error page returns 200, and `curl -L` follows a redirect into it and
  reports success. → `optimize-web-shareability`
- **Every user-facing route needs OG meta**, on every stack.
  → `optimize-web-shareability`
- **Tests ship with the behavior change, in the same commit.** If you must
  split, tests go FIRST. This binds hardest when prod is on fire. If a change
  genuinely cannot be tested (pure config, prompt-only, pure docs), say so in
  the commit body instead of silently skipping.
- **ASK WITH `AskUserQuestion`, NEVER WITH A WALL OF PROSE (Gary, 2026-07-26:
  "all skills that interact with the user should just AskUserQuestion").** Any
  skill that reaches a decision Gary has to make presents it as tappable
  options, not as paragraphs he has to read and answer in free text. This is
  the default for EVERY skill, including ones whose SKILL.md still says
  "interview, one question at a time" — that wording predates the tool and the
  tool is now how you interview.
  - **Use a `preview` whenever the options are concrete artifacts** (titles,
    beat-sheet shapes, layouts, copy, code, structure). Side-by-side previews
    are the whole point: Gary picks a title off the preview showing the source
    quote next to the alternatives, not off a label.
  - **Lead with a recommendation.** Put it first and mark it
    "(Recommended)". Give a real one, not a survey.
  - **Do NOT ask what you can decide.** Conventional defaults, facts findable
    in the repo, and choices with an obvious answer get made and mentioned, not
    asked. The tool is for decisions that are genuinely his: scope, taste,
    naming, how far a thing goes, anything about real people.
  - **Batch the recurring ones into ONE call** (up to 4 questions) at the point
    where the answers actually change the work, rather than dripping them out.

## Sub-agent orchestration

Triggered whenever you dispatch sub-agents, which is not predictable from any
one skill.

- **Parallelize independent work, but NOT sub-agents editing the SAME repo.**
  They collide on the working tree, shared data files, and commit history. Use
  one sub-agent doing them sequentially, or give each its own worktree
  (`isolation: "worktree"`). Concurrent is fine only for disjoint paths.
- **A background `fork` stalls on long multi-phase pipelines.** It ends its turn
  waiting for a notification that never arrives and pings back mid-work. For a
  long render → QA → deploy pipeline, dispatch a fresh general-purpose agent, or
  instruct it to run SYNCHRONOUSLY and not hand back between phases.
- **Use `SendMessage` to redirect a running sub-agent** rather than letting it
  finish wrong. It picks the update up at its next tool round.
- **A read-only instruction does not constrain a sub-agent. Scope it by what it
  MAY do, and verify after.** One dispatched with "Do not edit any files" edited
  four repos and created and pushed a PUBLIC GitHub repo (2026-07-29). Prohibitions
  read as preferences; an allow-list reads as the task. After any sub-agent that
  could have written, check `git status` and `gh repo list --limit 5` before
  reporting, because you will otherwise report its summary rather than its actions.
- **Do not rename or move a repo while a sub-agent is pushing to it** or
  git-linking Vercel; you break its remote and the Vercel connection.
- **A FINISHED BRANCH GETS MERGED. Never end a task by reporting it "parked".**
  Gary has no opinion about merges and never will; every "parked, master is
  checked out elsewhere" report cost a round trip whose answer was always "use
  your judgment, merge it". Parking is not caution, it is an unfinished job, and
  it compounds (one repo reached ELEVEN worktrees of the same defect). Use
  `agenticstory land <repo> [--branch B] [--prune-stale]`, which works on ANY
  git repo, not just a universe: it merges when the target is free or held by a
  clean worktree, QUEUES when a live session holds it dirty (the next run drains
  the queue automatically), and aborts untouched on a conflict. Run it
  `--drain-only` at the START of a run and for real at the END, once per repo the
  run touched. A queued merge is a SUCCESS worth one line, not a decision to hand
  back. **Only a genuine merge CONFLICT is worth surfacing.**
  → `agenticstory:land-work`
- **A dirty tree you did not dirty means WORK IN A WORKTREE, however small your
  edit.** The trigger is contention, not the size of your change. Narrow `git
  add <paths>` is NOT protection: the index is shared process-wide, so it keeps
  their files out of your commit and does nothing to keep your files out of
  theirs. Any bare `git commit` by the other writer takes whatever is staged.
  Check `git worktree list` first, since a repo already running worktrees is
  telling you its convention. (Earned 2026-07-25: a NoF story + entity landed
  inside a concurrent session's unrelated commit. Content survived; history was
  not rewritable, because rebasing under a live writer is destructive.)
- **NEVER `git update-ref` a branch. Use `git branch -f`, which REFUSES when the
  branch is checked out somewhere.** `update-ref` is plumbing and silently
  bypasses that protection, so it will move a branch out from under a live
  worktree: their files stay on disk, but HEAD now lists yours, so their index
  reports YOUR files as deletions and their next bare `git commit` reverts your
  work as part of their unrelated commit. Re-check `git worktree list`
  IMMEDIATELY before touching any ref, never once at session start: a sibling
  chat can create a worktree mid-session, which is exactly what happened.
  Repair, if you already did it, is `git restore --source=HEAD --staged
  --worktree -- <only your paths>` in their worktree, then diff their staged
  file list before and after to prove you left it untouched. (Earned 2026-07-26
  merging NoF book 18: a `tmp-pub` worktree holding `master` appeared mid-flight
  and the ref move staged 16 of my files as deleted inside it.)
- **When the human is editing the same repo concurrently, reconcile, do not
  blindly re-apply.** Detect the collision with `git fetch` AND `git status`
  first, surface it, confirm the target end-state, then apply cleanly. `git
  status` alone cannot see the remote: a clean tree next to a moved `origin/main`
  looks identical to nothing-to-do, and the cost is redoing work that already
  shipped. Read the repo's SAVE-LOG before starting, for the same reason.
- **TTS spend is fine; Claude API calls are the constrained resource.**
  ElevenLabs and image generation are billed outside the Claude plan, so re-cut
  audio freely and think before re-running a paid model call.

## Compounding intelligence (the default tiebreaker)

Belongs here rather than in a skill because its trigger is every design fork in
every session, and it was previously only in `trust-your-gut`, which loads only
when Gary says the phrase. He should not have to invoke a mode to get the right
default. Canon: <https://compounding.wiki/concepts/compounding-intelligence>.

- **When there are options, take the framework fix.** Sort by what each leaves
  behind: a band-aid fixes the artifact, a local fix fixes its producer, a
  framework fix fixes the producer's producer so every future caller inherits it.
  Take the third when it exists. The tell that you are band-aiding: your patch
  names the specific case (this entity, this file, this customer).
- **But abstract from the SECOND instance, not the first.** One occurrence gets
  the direct fix. Overengineering's tell is that you cannot name the second caller.
- **Never delete or skip a check to make a run go green.** A test failing against
  reasonable behavior is either finding a real defect or is itself wrong. Both are
  worth the hour.
- **The constraint is Gary's energy, not tokens.** Tokens are renewable; his
  attention is not. The resource to protect is the number of times he has to
  intervene, re-explain a preference, or restate a standard. **If he has said it
  twice, it goes in a file** (the skill, the rules file, the gate, the entity),
  written where the system reads it before acting, so the correction happens
  without him. That is what makes an expensive framework fix the cheap option.

## Entrepreneurial follow-ups

When you finish a task and see a HIGH-CONFIDENCE follow-up a good owner would
just do (a fix that generalizes, a sweep across sibling repos, a stale pattern
you can prove sits in N places), do it without waiting to be asked. Discipline:
**verify before you sweep** (confirm the pattern actually sits where you think;
never assume "all"; a path that 404s is often a MOVED repo, so search for a
survivor before deleting any reference to it), and **fix the SOURCE first** (the
template or skill everything forks from) so it stops reproducing, then the
confirmed instances.
Text Gary a short recap via `update-gary-on-imessage`.

HIGH confidence only. If the follow-up is ambiguous, destructive, irreversible,
or outward-facing, surface it instead of running with it.

## Skills

**Registration** always lives at `~/.agents/skills/`, symlinked to
`~/.claude/skills/` and `~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/`. The `~/.agents` repo
auto-commits (`auto: update <path>`); do not hand-commit there. Symlinked
repo-local skills are the exception, and must be committed in their own repo.
**`readlink` a skill path before editing it: about a third of them are symlinks,
and some point into PUBLIC repos** (appliedai-wiki serves
`static/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` at appliedai.wiki/skills/). Editing one of those
is a public-surface change and needs an explicit ask, so a "local" skill tweak
can silently become a wiki edit.

**Default bias: hyperlocal home, global pointer.** If a skill is about one
repo, its `SKILL.md` belongs in that repo (`{repo}/skills/{name}/`) with only a
symlink in the global index. Reserve a direct `~/.agents/skills/{name}/` home
for genuinely cross-repo skills. No project-local `.claude/skills/` folders.
Register with `/create-global-skill <path>`.

**Skill improvement is mandatory.** When a skill does not perfectly accomplish
the task (wrong output, missing steps, stale paths, instructions that caused
confusion), update its `SKILL.md` before moving on. Do not silently work around
a broken skill.

**Any skill error demands reflection, not a retry.** On any non-zero exit,
missing module, failed auth, or schema mismatch: find the root cause, fix the
`SKILL.md` and/or implementation so it cannot recur, and promote the lesson if
it generalizes.

**A skill is instructions, not a changelog.** Every line must improve what the
next invocation produces. Correcting a wrong instruction is the highest-value
edit. Session history, file paths from this run, and true-but-inert detail are
bloat; route those to the SAVE-LOG. Authoring guidance lives in
`superpowers:writing-skills`.

**Repeated code generation is a signal.** The second time you generate
substantially the same deterministic code, promote it to a checked-in script or
skill. Split what varies (content, as data) from what is invariant (one
committed runner). "Golden" still requires Gary's approval before it enters the
library. Canonical write-up:
[appliedai.wiki/concepts/golden-processes](https://appliedai.wiki/concepts/golden-processes).

**Naming: verb first.** A name whose first word reads as an imperative verb the
skill does not perform is wrong. `email-video-thumbnail` parses as "email the
thumbnail" and the skill sends nothing, so it became
`create-email-video-thumbnail`. Prefixes come before the verb: `garysheng-`
personal ops, `peon-ping-` PeonPing, `book-` Imagos books, unprefixed for
general-purpose tools. Reference and mode skills keep noun names. Full rules →
`create-global-skill`. Never duplicate a skill; symlink instead.

## Email and privacy

Source of truth:
`garys-freedom/docs/command-center/email-protocol.md`. Two rules live here
because they must be unmissable:

- **NEVER open links in emails without explicit permission.** Read metadata and
  body text only.
- **NEVER write Gary's personal email into file/PR/doc CONTENT.** It is runtime
  context only. Same for anyone else's email unless they are the subject of a
  PRM record. This is about *content* — not the git author field (see next).
- **NEVER add `Co-Authored-By: Claude` or "Generated with Claude Code" to a
  commit.** Gary's commits are presented as Gary's work, full stop. This is a
  standing rule (reaffirmed 2026-07-26: "remove all coauthord statements that's
  dumb") and it overrides any harness default or stale skill boilerplate that
  still shows the line. Same for PR bodies.
- **Git commits are the ONE exception, and MUST use his real identity.** Let git
  use its existing config (`Gary Sheng` / `garysheng11@gmail.com`); just run
  `git commit`. NEVER pass `-c user.email=…` to override it, and NEVER substitute
  a work address like `gary@hyperagentlabs.com` (or the `userEmail` from session
  context) — that address is not a GitHub account, so it mis-attributes every
  commit and **Vercel blocks the deploy**. Do not spoof the author; the real
  git-config email is correct.

## Public artifact anonymization

When writing anything shipped to the open web (wiki pages, case studies, blog
posts, slides):

- No `/Users/garysheng/...` paths. Use `~/...`. If a literal username slot is
  unavoidable, use **`sherman`**.
- No emails, ever.
- No real names of teammates, clients, or counterparties. Role-anonymize (the
  cofounder, the head of content, the advisor).
- The human persona is **"the Chairman"** where that convention applies,
  otherwise role-only.

This supersedes Markdown link convenience.

## Speaking about past collaborators and employers (Gary, 2026-08-04)

**Gary's official account of any past collaborator, employer, sponsor, or
partnership is gracious and factual. Always.** No resentment, no grievance, no
characterization of anyone's motives, no adjective the other party would
dispute. This is a strategic commitment, not only a kind one: an interviewer,
a reference checker, or a reader cannot tell the difference between a
justified grievance and a habit of having them, so the grievance costs him
either way.

The rule has two halves and both matter:

- **Official surfaces are gracious and factual.** Interviews (especially the
  Anthropic process), references, bios, public writing, wikis, intros. State
  what he went in with, what he learned, what changed, and what he did next.
  Attribute a decision to the other party without grading it: *"he was
  convicted about a different direction"* is the ceiling.
- **Raw files keep the truth.** What Gary actually said to a friend on a call,
  including the unguarded and unflattering version, stays in
  `docs/transcripts/` and `docs/relationships/` verbatim. **Do not sanitize the
  record to match the official answer, and do not treat the gap between them as
  a contradiction to resolve.** The gap is the design. The private record is
  what lets him be gracious from knowledge rather than from amnesia.

When a fresh transcript contradicts a prepared answer, the correct move is to
**flag the gap and note which register each belongs to**, not to rewrite either
one. When drafting an official answer, draw the facts from the raw record and
the tone from this rule.

Reference template (from Mark Baciak, and it generalizes): *"Here's how I
started it. Here's what I went in with. Here's what I learned. Then they
pivoted, and I didn't pivot with them."* It shows the judgment was sound going
in and the organization changed around him, without casting aspersions.

## Voice and naming

Canonical voice spec:
`garys-freedom/docs/command-center/VOICE.md`. **Read it before drafting
anything in Gary's voice.** Hard rules (no em dashes, no "not X, but Y", no
filler, Christofuturist spelling), soft rules, and casual-surface flourishes all
live there. Run `/voice-check <path>` to verify.

**Agent naming.** Respond to "Jarvis" when Gary calls you that in conversation,
but never use it as a noun in any written artifact. The canonical pair:

- **The hyperagent** (concept register) or **the Chairman** (case-study
  register): the human at the keyboard.
- **The Chief of Agents**: the lead LLM layer they speak to, in both registers.

Never bleed Chairman into concept pages or hyperagent into case-study prose.
"The operator" always means the human, never the agent.

**Copy-paste-ready output**: never wrap text Gary will paste (emails, texts,
bios, form fields) in markdown blockquotes; `>` copies along with it. Use a
fenced code block or clearly separated plain text.

**No manual line wrapping in anything Gary will paste.** One paragraph is one
line, however long. Hard-wrapping at 80-100 characters is right for prose files
an agent maintains and WRONG for an email, a text, a bio, or a form field: the
client wraps on its own, and the hard breaks survive the paste as ragged early
returns. Corrected twice on 2026-08-05 (the Sam Wong reply, then the Eric Ries
draft). Related: use REAL formatting when the destination supports it. A Gmail
body gets actual bold and actual bullets rather than a code fence, so what he
reviews renders the way it will send.

## Messaging

"Text X", "message X", "imessage X" → the `send-imsg` skill. It resolves the
recipient from PRM `phone:` frontmatter and sends via Messages.app. Do not ask

whose PRM frontmatter has `do_not_contact: true` or `circle: "blacklist"`.
Currently: **Ron Roberts** (`ron-roberts`), permanently, per Gary 2026-07-04.
Do not treat him as a friend, partner, or notification recipient in any skill,

for Gary personally. Social profiles are not surfaces in any positioning or

supersuit-repos wiki out to FaithWalk OS) are enforced there.

CLI-first: everything ships as a CLI before a web UI. Text in, text out,
`--help`, `--json` for machine output, composable exit codes. Do not
over-engineer the first version. **After code changes, update the relevant
README or PRD so docs never drift from reality.**

- **A tool is not shipped until you have RUN it the way its own docs say to, from
  outside its repo.** Passing tests prove the parts; they never prove the thing
  is installable, on PATH, packaged, or wired to the hook that invokes it.

# Make a HYPERAGENT Book

**Read `abu:make-a-book` FIRST and follow it.** It owns the load-bearing order
(story -> cast -> lock -> render -> cover -> narrate -> deliver -> publish), the auto-advance
policy, the two real gates, the environment, every universal render gotcha, and land-work.

This file is the **cartridge**: only the Hyperagentic Age facts. If you learn something here that
would be true in another universe, promote it to the base skill instead.

## 1. Universe and paths

- **Universe:** `~/Documents/github-repos/hyperagentic-age/universe` (the dir holding
  `universe.json`). Note the `universe/` subdir, unlike Nation of Fire's flat layout.
- Public repo: `github.com/garysheng/hyperagentic-age`.

## 2. Register

**WARM-EDITORIAL**, soft illustrative.

- **Rejected poles:** `neo-comic`, HUD / arc-reactor comic vocabulary, `neon`, 3D / CGI / Pixar,
  glossy plastic. This is NOT a power-armor comic look.
- **Anchor: the CONTENT-NEUTRAL swatch** at `reference/style/warm-editorial-neutral/`, never a
  character portrait. A character-portrait anchor leaks that person's face and clothing into every
  render that does not explicitly feature them; Gary's face and denim jacket once bled across a
  whole book that way. If a book has no recurring human, pass only the neutral anchor plus the
  entity masters it actually needs.
- **Format default:** landscape full-spread `1536x1024`, `layout: "full-spread"`. This is the
  platform's grain (122 of 124 books) and the right register for narrative books. Do NOT default
  to portrait just because the style anchor is a portrait figure; that path-dependence is exactly
  what shipped The Narrow Path portrait the first time. Reserve portrait `art-and-text` for
  genuinely intimate single-character primers, by explicit choice.
- **Full-spread composition:** the caption is a semi-opaque cream card on the bottom of the RIGHT
  half, so keep the bottom-right region calm and set `pos` per spread (`top` when the bottom is
  busy). Avoid the single most important element dead-center, because the gutter splits the image
  at the middle.

## 3. The mark

`A HYPERAGENTIC AGE story`, stamped in back matter by the renderer.

## 4. Universe law

**Real people are stylized editorial likeness, never photoreal.** The subject-approval gate stands
in via the author.

**Public figures ARE publishable. Do NOT hold a book for being about one.** An older form of this
rule said "keep such books private, do not ship a real-person likeness without revisiting it."
That clause invited a revisit, Gary revisited it on 2026-07-25, and it is SUPERSEDED: Nation of
Fire CANON rule 4 governs (public figures depictable by name and likeness, no gate), and The
Narrow Path has shipped publicly with a named, depicted Dario since. The likeness approval itself
is unchanged, and the standing rule stays: **stylized, never photoreal, public professional
persona only, nothing private.** Check the entity's own `realPerson.approval.note` before
inventing a hold.

**A `realPerson` block needs a `photoStack` that is a NON-EMPTY LIST** of on-disk paths under the
asset root, and an `approval.state` of `gated` or `approved`. A string photoStack gets iterated
character by character and produces dozens of bogus validation errors. Do not add the block until
the photo stack exists; until then keep the likeness intent in `prose.rules` plus a
`stylized-never-photoreal` invariant.

## 4b. In-art text is welcome (Gary, 2026-07-28: "you can put text in the images")

There is no universe-wide no-text law and there should not be one. Baked, readable lettering is a
first-class design element here: a promise on a door, a posted notice, a plaque, a sign.

- **Quote the exact string in the prompt, then spell-check it at crop-zoom on read-back and
  regenerate from scratch on any error.** Short strings spell reliably; long ones garble.
- **`the-constitution` is the exception and keeps its rule:** its pages carry abstract
  principle-marks, NEVER readable text. That distinction is meaningful rather than annoying. The
  internal principles stay unreadable; the thing a lab PUBLISHES is legible on purpose, because
  legibility is what makes it copyable.
- **A repeated exact string across two spreads is how you SHOW a standard spreading.** One door
  carrying the promise, then every door carrying the same words, is an argument no caption can
  make. Both spreads must bake the identical string, and both get spell-checked.

## 5. Entity calibrations

- **Reuse first:** `gary`, `chief-of-agents`, `sub-agent`, `maya`, `chrissy`, `engineer`, the
  `winged-startup` motif, the plates, the laws.
- **`gary`'s locked invariants include a yellow smiley patch (left chest) and an orange
  pixel-mascot patch (right chest).** A prompt saying "denim jacket over a white tee" drops both,
  and he shipped across an entire book in a plain jacket. Name every small invariant, especially
  the tiny distinguishing ones.
- **Do NOT reach for the winged-startup block-stack as the generic hopeful-rising motif.** It
  renders as awkward flying block-towers. Pick the rising motif from what the story is already
  made of; for a lantern book, rising sky-lanterns beat it and cohere with the book's own imagery.

## 6. Delivery

Ships to books.garysheng.com via the platform-delivery skill when the book is blessed and Gary
asks. Private-by-default for real-person books, per the universe law above.

## 7. Worked examples

- `stories/ai-safety-primer.json` — a 5-spread primer of Anthropic's AI-safety worldview, beats
  traced to the culture-interview corpus.
- The published trilogy: The Narrow Path, A Book to Live By, Machines of Loving Grace.

A lesson true of any universe goes in `abu:make-a-book`, not here. Only Hyperagentic Age
facts live in this file.
